jobs.description: Libertex Group Overview Established in 1997, the Libertex Group has helped shape the online trading industry by merging innovative technology, market movements and digital trends. The multi-awarded online trading platform, Libertex, enables traders to access the market and invest in stocks or trade CFDs with underlying assets being commodities, Forex, ETFs, cryptocurrencies, and others. A firm believer in the power of sports to inspire, empower and push for success, Libertex is the Official Online Trading Partner of Audi Revolut F1® Team. We build innovative fintech so people can #TradeForMore with Libertex. Job Overview We are looking for a System Business Analyst in the data department to bridge communication between our business and development teams, translating business needs into clear technical specifications. Responsibilities: Collaborate with stakeholders to identify, analyze, and document business requirements. Translate business needs into acceptance criteria and technical specifications for the development team. Analyze, define, and document detailed system requirements, including functional, non-functional, and integration requirements. Lead system configuration and data mapping efforts, particularly those involving APIs, third-party platforms, and internal system integrations. Support post-release validation and acceptance of features to ensure solutions meet stakeholder expectations. 3+ years of experience as a Business Analyst or Systems Analyst Background in IT or software development Experience in product and marketing analytics Strong SQL skills for querying and analyzing data Solid experience in gathering, analyzing, and documenting business requirements Experience creating data flow diagrams (DFDs) and data architecture diagrams Familiarity with API documentation tools and a basic understanding of REST API concepts Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills Excellent communication skills Spoken English at B2 level or higher Tech Stack Databases and data warehouses: ClickHouse, Redshift, PostgreSQL, BigQuery Analytics and marketing platforms: Mixpanel, GA4, AppsFlyer, Blueshift Data pipelines and streaming: RudderStack, Kafka Nice to Have Hands-on experience with data warehouses such as ClickHouse, BigQuery, or Redshift Experience in FinTech, especially CFD trading Familiarity with AI tools for analytics, such as MCP servers and skills Experience with Python or JavaScript Quarterly bonuses based on Company performance 24 working days of annual leave Udemy Business unlimited membership & language training courses Professional and personal development opportunities in a fast-growing environment Libertex Group is an equal opportunity employer, fostering an inclusive and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on any characteristic protected by the law. Candidate privacy is respected, and all data is securely stored and used solely for recruitment purposes, in line with GDPR and our internal policies. Unsuccessful applicants may have their data retained for future opportunities unless deletion is requested.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description: Company Overview Voted #1 EHR by PC Mag, WRS Health delivers a fully integrated cloud based EMR and practice management solutions to its clients. We bring solutions to physicians by providing constant enhancement of our products and services including EHR, practice management, marketing, patient coordination and billing. Job Purpose and Role The Technical Product Owner (TPO) acts as the bridge between business objectives and technical execution, ensuring that products are developed in alignment with strategic goals and technical standards. As the primary advocate for the customer, the TPO works closely with UI/UX architects, developers, and stakeholders to deliver high-quality, value-driven product releases. This role is responsible for guiding the product lifecycle from concept to launch and beyond, ensuring that user needs are met while maintaining technical integrity. As a key leader, the TPO is ultimately accountable for the product’s success and continuous alignment with both business and user expectations. Prior experience in healthcare or healthcare-focused software is considered an advantage. Key Responsibilities Product Ownership & Agile Leadership Act as the primary contact for major system issues and product-related inquiries. Gather and document requirements from clients and internal stakeholders. Manage and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring readiness for development. Lead Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, sprint reviews, and other team meetings. Collaborat closely with developers and QA to ensure product quality, accurate implementation, and smooth releases. Communicate the value of new features to internal teams and clients. Oversee and mentor the Product Owner team, including goal-setting, project assignments, and performance evaluations. Maintain internal tools such as developer PTO and assignment trackers. Regulatory Compliance Handle system certification processes (e.g., ONC, Surescripts, MDToolbox/DEA). Ensure ongoing compliance with healthcare regulations and industry standards. Manual Testing Team Oversight Managed structure and productivity of the manual testing team. Aligned testing timelines with product delivery schedules. Provided regular performance feedback. Clinical Services (MIPS) Oversight Directed MIPS Services in line with financial and strategic objectives. Ensured regulatory compliance and managed escalations. Coordinated with Reg-ent and leadership, delivered financial reporting, and trained new staff on MIPS-related tasks. Qualifications Proven experience conducting user research and synthesizing insights through user flows, personas, and other methodologies. Experience in the healthcare or health technology industry related to medical practices Demonstrated ability to manage conflicting priorities, distinguish between critical roadblocks and distractions, and make sound decisions under pressure. Strong data-driven mindset with experience leveraging analytics to inform product decisions. Proactive and self-motivated, with the judgment to know when to seek guidance. Extensive experience gathering, documenting, and communicating detailed requirements, including functional, technical, reporting, and data needs. Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to influence and build consensus across diverse teams and stakeholders. Deep experience working in Agile environments, breaking down epics into actionable stories, and guiding teams through the software development lifecycle. Track record of successful technology product design, implementation, and delivery. Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking abilities. Demonstrated leadership experience, including team management and mentoring. Proficiency with Jira and cloud-based architectures. This is an Independent Contractor position. Job Type: Full-time Remote Hours: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM EST or 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM EST This job description is intended to describe the general requirements for the position.

jobs.title: Product Manager at Tratta
jobs.description: About Tratta Tratta is the platform that powers credit and collections at scale, and we try to make it enjoyable to work on. Our clients are collection agencies and law firms recovering debt from consumers. Their account data lands in Tratta and is mapped and validated on the way in. They run email and SMS campaigns off it. Consumers land on a payment portal carrying the client's brand, where they can pay, negotiate a plan or sign an agreement electronically without ever speaking to a collector. Payments clear through us by card, ACH or check, and it all feeds back into reporting that shapes the next campaign. Campaigns, data and payments as one closed loop instead of four vendors stitched together. Every week that loop moves millions of dollars in payments, ingests nearly 100 million rows of client data and serves almost 10 million API requests. About the Product Team The product team is small: two PMs, one designer and a distributed engineering team of about ten. You would be our second product hire. There is no product ops layer, no analyst and no one sitting between you and the client, or between you and the code. The role You will own a set of topics end to end. Not "manage a backlog" in the abstract, but pick up messy input from clients and customer success, turn it into something the team can build, get it shipped, and then make sure it actually gets used. Turn requests into work. Client and CS requests arrive as symptoms, not specs. You dig into what is actually being asked, decide whether it is a bug, a gap, a training problem or a real product need, and write it up so a developer can pick it up without a meeting. Prioritize. You decide what gets built next among a lot of competing, legitimate asks, and you can explain the reasoning to a client, a developer and a founder in three different ways. Firefight. Bugs and urgent client issues will land on you. You triage, reproduce, escalate the real ones, and close the loop with whoever raised it. Discovery. You help figure out what we should build next, from client conversations, usage data and your own read of the market. Data. You are comfortable with data end to end: getting it, questioning it, and deciding what to do about it. Own outcomes, not output. Shipping is the midpoint, not the finish line. If a feature launches and nobody knows it exists or nobody adopts it, that is your problem to solve. You will write the client email, record the walkthrough, check the numbers a month later and tell us honestly whether it worked. Wear multiple hats. Small changes you can do yourself with Claude, you do yourself. Otherwise: specs, debugging, data and dashboards, release notes, client emails, whatever the topic needs. There is no one to hand it to. What this role is not It is not a role where you write requirements and hand them to someone else. It is not a role with a defined scope that stays defined. And it is not a role where you can be effective while waiting to be told what to do. How we work Very little process and very few meetings. No planning ritual that exists to justify the previous planning ritual. If something is not working, we change it the next day. The tradeoff is that nothing will be handed to you. There is no queue of pre-groomed tickets, no one checking whether you did the thing, and no process to hide behind if a topic quietly stalls. Autonomy and accountability come as a pair here. We use Claude heavily across product work: analysis, drafting, prototyping, bulk operations across Linear, Slack, HubSpot and our data. Being fluent with AI tooling is not a bonus point, it is how the job gets done at this team size. You will do well here if you Have shipped real product in a small team Are comfortable being close to the technical detail: reading logs, querying data, understanding an API contract, reproducing a bug before you file it Write clearly and briefly Prefer deciding with 70% of the information over waiting for 100% Are direct.
